notice: The line that leaves configuration mode after a refused SSH line (D-358, action-templates 9.3). Data, not Go literals (D-58): the core knows connection kinds, not vendors. The writer looks back from the refused line for the nearest line that entered configuration mode and was not closed again by a later line 'end' (lowercased, runs of spaces collapsed, matched like cli-ban.json: the start of the line, at a word end); the first rule whose 'enter' matches gives the line it types, once, then the session closes. Every block closed: nothing is typed. Only a line that never saves what is pending may be listed here: where a vendor has an abort form it is that one. No rule matches: nothing is typed and the session just closes, as before D-358.

rules.why: Cisco IOS / IOS-XE and Aruba AOS-CX: a line in global configuration and its ordinary sub-modes (interface, access list) takes effect when it is typed and there is no candidate to commit, so end only returns to the exec prompt. Sub-modes that hold changes until they are left are rules of their own below (MST). Cisco IOS-XR (configure terminal is a candidate there): end with uncommitted changes asks yes/no/cancel and the writer never answers it; the session closes and the candidate is dropped.

Cisco IOS / IOS-XE and NX-OS MST region sub-mode: the region changes are pending until the sub-mode is left, and exit or end APPLY them; abort leaves it without applying. The nearest enter line wins, so inside this sub-mode abort goes out, not end.

FortiOS: a config block is saved by next and end, so end would save a half-typed entry; abort leaves the edit and the config shell without saving. On a device where 'config' means something else (AOS-CX shorthand) abort is an unknown command, which changes nothing.
